text: When is cyber monday: Nov. 30, 2026, the Monday after Thanksgiving. Cyber Monday 2026 falls on Monday, November 30. It is the Monday after Thanksgiving (Nov. 26) and three days after Black Friday (Nov. 27). Retailers use it for online-only discounts, and in recent years it has been the biggest online shopping day of the year in the U.S.. With Black Friday on Nov. 27, 2026, retailers have already started early holiday sales, and shoppers are checking the Cyber Monday date.. The name was coined in 2005 by Shop.org, part of the National Retail Federation, after retailers noticed a jump in online orders on the Monday after Thanksgiving. Because it follows Thanksgiving, the date moves each year and always falls between Nov. 26 and Dec. 2. In 2027 it will be Nov. 29. Cyber Monday 2025 (Dec. 1, 2025) set a record of $14.25 billion in U.S. Online spending, according to Adobe Analytics, making it the biggest online shopping day ever. For the 2026 season, Adobe forecast $275.1 billion in U.S. Online sales from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31. Many deals now start well before the day itself. Walmart announced three holiday sales events running from Nov. 12 through Dec. 2, 2026, and Target scheduled an early Black Friday sale for Nov. 5–7, 2026. Many stores keep Cyber Monday prices going for the rest of that week, often called Cyber Week.

Who is Scott Colom? Mississippi Democrat in the 2026 Senate race. Scott Colom is a Democrat and local prosecutor from Mississippi who is challenging Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith for a U.S. Senate seat in the 2026 midterm election. After the Nov. 3, 2026 vote he held a narrow lead of about 1,100 votes, but as of Nov. 5 the race had not been called and ballots were still being counted.. The Mississippi Senate race is one of the closest contests of the 2026 midterms. Colom led Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes on Nov. 4, with mail and affidavit ballots still to be counted.. Colom has been district attorney for Mississippi's 16th Judicial District, based in Lowndes County, since 2016. He won the Democratic primary with about 73% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, a Republican, was seeking a second full term. No Democrat has won a U.S. Senate seat in Mississippi in nearly four decades, and forecasters had rated the race safely Republican. The result turned out far closer. Early on Nov. 4 Colom led by just 43 votes. By Wednesday night, Nov. 4, with about 96% of the expected vote counted, unofficial results showed Colom at 464,926 votes (49.0%), Hyde-Smith at 463,788 (48.9%) and independent Ty Pinkins at about 2.1%. No major outlet had called the race. Thousands of ballots were still pending. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive through Nov. 10; the Secretary of State's office said about 3,600 were outstanding. Affidavit (provisional) ballots are still being reviewed, and Colom's campaign estimated about 15,000 of them. Counties must certify results by Nov. 13. Mississippi has no runoff for this race, since the candidate with the most votes wins, and it has no automatic or requested recount; a losing candidate can examine ballot materials and challenge the result in court. Both sides say they expect to win. Colom said the ballots still being counted favor him, while Hyde-Smith's campaign said it was closely monitoring the count and remained confident once every legally cast vote is counted. Lawyers for both campaigns are watching the count.
